Select unrelated individuals at random

Source: R/rkn_select_random.R
rkn_select_random.Rd

Selects a maximum set of unrelated individuals, a set with no related pair of the largest possible size (see rkn_selection), and makes at random the choices that the network leaves open. The network is partitioned into families, its connected components, and each family is resolved on its own: since no relationship crosses two families, the union of their selections has no related pair. Structural rules decide most individuals; those left undecided in large families are resolved by an exact algorithm that also handles the intricate families of genetic isolates (see the section Search over maximum sets of rkn_selection).

Usage

rkn_select_random(g, uniform = FALSE, seed = NULL, diagnostics = TRUE)

Arguments

g

An igraph object. Vertex names must be stored in V(g)$name. Vertex attributes cannot be named degree, max_path_length or .name: these names are reserved for the structural measures computed during the selection. The network is usually built with rkn_graph_from_kinship, which also checks the samples; for a network built in another way, see rkn_check_samples.

uniform

Logical. If FALSE (default), structural rules decide most individuals and the remaining choices are made at random; the result is a maximum set, but the maximum sets are not equally likely, and the rules never choose some of them: in a chain of six relatives, two of its four maximum sets. If TRUE, each family is drawn uniformly at random among all its maximum sets, so that every maximum set of the network has the same probability, and the selection probabilities are exact: with diagnostics, node_diagnostics$inclusion_probability gives the probability that each individual is selected. Families too intricate for this exact computation are selected as with uniform = FALSE and reported in the column uniform of family_summary (see rkn_selection).

seed

Optional integer. If provided, the selection is reproducible: a seed is drawn from it for each family, so that the selection within a family does not depend on the random numbers used by the others, and different values give independent selections. If NULL (default), the current random number stream is used.

diagnostics

Logical. If TRUE (default), the returned object also records how each individual and each family was resolved (node_diagnostics and family_summary), which print(), summary() and plot(type = "diagnostics") use. Diagnostics increase the run time and the size of the returned object; on very large networks, diagnostics = FALSE returns the selection alone.

Value

An object of class rkn_selection, with print, summary and plot methods; $kept holds the identifiers of the selected individuals.

See also

rkn_selection, summary.rkn_selection, plot.rkn_selection, rkn_select_criteria, rkn_select_global.

Examples

# A small relatedness network: two parents and their child (P1, P2, C1), a pair of
# siblings (S1, S2), three mutually related individuals (T1, T2, T3), a larger family
# (parents D1 and D2, their children K1 and K2, and K3, born to D2 and D3, a
# half-sibling of K1 and K2) and an unrelated individual (U1).
g <- igraph::graph_from_literal(P1 - C1 - P2, S1 - S2, T1 - T2 - T3 - T1,
                                D1 - K1 - D2, D1 - K2 - D2, K1 - K2,
                                D2 - K3 - D3, K1 - K3, K2 - K3, U1)
sex <- c(P1 = "F", C1 = "M", P2 = "M", S1 = "M", S2 = "F", T1 = "M", T2 = "F", T3 = "M",
         D1 = "M", K1 = "F", D2 = "F", K2 = "M", K3 = "F", D3 = "M", U1 = "F")
age <- c(P1 = 52, C1 = 21, P2 = 55, S1 = 34, S2 = 31, T1 = 60, T2 = 33, T3 = 29,
         D1 = 63, K1 = 35, D2 = 61, K2 = 38, K3 = 30, D3 = 58, U1 = 44)
igraph::V(g)$sex <- unname(sex[igraph::V(g)$name])
igraph::V(g)$age <- unname(age[igraph::V(g)$name])
sel <- rkn_select_random(g, seed = 1)
sel
#> <rkn_selection> Random selection, seed 1
#> Call: rkn_select_random(g = g, seed = 1)
#> Individuals: 15 | selected: 8 (53.3%)
#> Families: 5 | size min/mean/max: 1 / 3.00 / 6
#> Families with up to 5 members: 4 | with 6 or more: 1
#> Families resolved by a search over maximum sets: 1
sel$kept
#> [1] "P1" "P2" "S2" "T3" "D3" "D1" "D2" "U1"
summary(sel)
#> <rkn_selection summary> Random selection, seed 1
#> Individuals: 15 | selected: 8 (53.3%) | families: 5
#> 
#> Selection by family structure:
#>  size                               structure families individuals selected
#>     1                       single individual        1           1        1
#>     2                            related pair        1           2        1
#>     3 chain of three (e.g. parents and child)        1           3        2
#>     3                  three mutually related        1           3        1
#>     6             family of 6 or more members        1           6        3
#> 
#> Individuals by type of decision and outcome:
#>                                  outcome
#> decision                          selected discarded
#>   kept without a choice                  6         0
#>   discarded without a choice             0         4
#>   decided among single candidates        2         3
#>   decided among alternative sets         0         0

# The selection alone, without diagnostics
rkn_select_random(g, seed = 1, diagnostics = FALSE)$kept
#> [1] "P1" "P2" "S2" "T3" "D3" "D1" "D2" "U1"

# Uniformly among all the maximum sets, with the probability that each individual is
# selected
u <- rkn_select_random(g, uniform = TRUE, seed = 1)
u
#> <rkn_selection> Uniform random selection, seed 1
#> Call: rkn_select_random(g = g, uniform = TRUE, seed = 1)
#> Individuals: 15 | selected: 8 (53.3%)
#> Families: 5 | size min/mean/max: 1 / 3.00 / 6
#> Families with up to 5 members: 4 | with 6 or more: 1
#> Families sampled uniformly among their maximum sets: 5 of 5
#> Maximum sets: 6 in total; families with more than one: 2 of 5
#> Two uniform draws differ on average in 1.2 of the 8 selected individuals (14.6%)
u$node_diagnostics[, c("id", "inclusion_probability")]
#>    id inclusion_probability
#> 1  P1             1.0000000
#> 2  C1             0.0000000
#> 3  P2             1.0000000
#> 4  S1             0.5000000
#> 5  S2             0.5000000
#> 6  T1             0.3333333
#> 7  T2             0.3333333
#> 8  T3             0.3333333
#> 9  D1             1.0000000
#> 10 K1             0.0000000
#> 11 D2             1.0000000
#> 12 K2             0.0000000
#> 13 K3             0.0000000
#> 14 D3             1.0000000
#> 15 U1             1.0000000
